app.title: Vigia
nav.label: Sections
confirm.act: Vigia will delete messages and time people out on its own. Start moderating?
warn.jev-unavailable: Jev is not answering. Messages pass unmoderated until it's back.
warn.dropped: Chat is very busy: some highlight checks were skipped.
warn.halted: Vigia stopped because Jev rejected the API key. Set a new key and restart Vigia.
live.empty.title: Waiting for chat
live.empty.body: Messages appear here as Vigia reads them, with what each rule thought.
spoiler.noHighlight: Possible spoilers are never shown on stream
spoiler.topics: Protected topics (the streamer never sees these)
spoiler.topics.placeholder: One per line, for example: who the final boss is
spoiler.topics.none: No protected topics. Your mods can add some without you ever reading them.
spoiler.topics.count: {n} protected topics, added by your mods
spoiler.pack.help: Only the part names are shown here. Topics from earlier parts stop being protected once you pass them.
spoiler.pack.none: No community spoiler pack for this category. Anyone can write one: see spoiler-packs/README.md.
screen.title: On stream now
kind.question: Question
uncertain.intro: Jev wasn't sure about these, so Vigia did nothing. Decide here, or adjust the rule's thresholds.
uncertain.empty.title: Nothing uncertain
uncertain.empty.body: Messages Jev is unsure about land here instead of being guessed.
highlights.intro.auto: Jev's picks go straight to the overlay. These are the ones it was less sure about.
highlights.intro.approve: Nothing reaches the overlay until a mod picks it here.
highlights.empty.title: No suggestions yet
highlights.empty.body: Questions and notable messages from chat will show up here.
rules.intro: Each rule is one yes-or-no question for Jev. Changes apply at once and are saved to vigia.yaml.
rules.preview.none: No recent messages to compare yet.
rules.preview: Of the last {n} messages, {act} would trigger it and {unsure} would go to Uncertain.
rules.preview.highlight: Of the last {n} messages, {act} would be highlighted and {unsure} suggested.
pack.antispoiler: Plot spoilers for the game on stream
test.label: Try a message
test.placeholder: Type what a viewer might write
add.title: New rule
add.help: Write the question in plain words. English works best, but Spanish works too.
add.question: Question
add.question.placeholder: Does the message tell the streamer how to play without being asked?
add.no.placeholder: Reactions, jokes, answers to the streamer
raw.title: Edit vigia.yaml directly
raw.help: For everything the forms don't cover. Invalid files are refused and nothing changes.
settings.mode.auto: Show them on stream right away
settings.mode.approve: Wait for a mod to approve
settings.includeBroadcaster: Also consider the streamer's own messages
settings.exempt.help: Their messages can still be highlighted.
settings.mode.local: Only this computer can open the dashboard.
settings.mode.exposed: The dashboard is on the internet. Mods sign in with Twitch.
settings.adminCode: The admin code is printed in Vigia's logs when it starts.
overlay.title: OBS overlay
overlay.help: In OBS, add a Browser source with this address. The background is transparent.
overlay.secret: Keep this address private: it contains the overlay key.
stats.costNote: Estimated at $0.042 per million input tokens. Output is free.
audit.title: Activity
wizard.language.title: Welcome to Vigia
wizard.language.body: Vigia reads your chat with Jev, moderates it with your rules, and puts the best messages on stream. First, languages.
wizard.rules.title: Choose what Vigia watches for
wizard.rules.body: You can change these any time, and add your own questions in Rules.
wizard.spoilers.title: Spoiler protection
wizard.spoilers.body: Vigia uses your Twitch category as the game. Telling it how far you are is optional: it only makes it stricter about what comes later.
wizard.spoilers.none: The anti-spoiler rule is off. You can add it later in Rules.
wizard.overlay.title: Add the overlay to OBS
wizard.overlay.body: Highlighted questions and announcements appear here. Use Preview to place it before going live.
wizard.overlay.mods: The streamer sets up the overlay from their own account.
wizard.observe.title: Vigia starts by observing
wizard.observe.body: For now it only shows what it would do: nothing is deleted and nobody is timed out.
wizard.observe.note: When the Live tab shows decisions you agree with, click the lantern at the top and choose Start moderating for real.
login.title: Sign in to the dashboard
login.twitchHelp: For the streamer and the channel's moderators. Vigia only checks who you are.
login.codeHelp: Printed in Vigia's logs when it starts.
login.stateError: The Twitch sign-in didn't match this browser. Try again.
login.twitchDenied: Twitch didn't complete the sign-in. Try again.
setup.weak: This computer has no keychain Vigia can use, so your keys are saved without encryption in your user folder.
setup.unlock.title: Enter the setup code
setup.unlock.body: This Vigia can be reached from other computers, so only whoever can read its logs may set it up. The logs print the code when Vigia starts.
setup.unlock.wrong: That code is not right. Copy it from the logs, for example: docker compose logs vigia
setup.source.title: Where should Vigia watch?
setup.source.body: You can change this later by setting Vigia up again.
setup.source.twitch.help: Vigia moderates and highlights in your own chat. Needs a free Twitch app (about 5 minutes).
setup.source.observe.help: Try Vigia on any public channel. Read-only: it never writes, deletes or times out.
setup.app.title: Create your Twitch app
setup.app.body: Vigia talks to Twitch through an app registered to you, so everything stays under your account.
setup.app.step1: Open the Twitch developer console and sign in.
setup.app.name: Name
setup.app.step4: Create it, open Manage, and copy the Client ID.
setup.app.2fa: Twitch asks for two-factor authentication on your account before you can register apps.
setup.login.title: Log in to Twitch
setup.login.body: Vigia asks only for what it needs: reading and writing chat, deleting messages, timeouts and bans, and seeing your mods.
setup.login.opened: Your browser opened Twitch. Confirm this code there:
setup.login.waiting: Waiting for you to confirm. The code works for {minutes} minutes.
setup.login.openThis: Open Twitch and confirm this code:
setup.jev.title: Add your Jev key
setup.jev.body: Jev reads each message and answers your rules. The key is yours: usage is billed to your account, and it is stored encrypted on this computer.
setup.jev.body.server: Jev reads each message and answers your rules. The key is yours: usage is billed to your account. It is kept in Vigia's data folder, readable only by the user running Vigia.
setup.jev.whereLink: Get a Vercel AI Gateway key
setup.jev.error.badKey: Jev rejected the key. Check that it is complete and that your account has credit or a card.
setup.done.title: Vigia is ready
setup.done.body: Next, the dashboard walks you through your rules and the OBS overlay. Vigia starts by observing, so nothing is deleted until you say so.
